correctness.rationale: For every m,n>=1, vertices initially sharing a shore/color are synchronous twins; retaining one tagged representative per initially occupied color gives an exact finite quotient for microscopic trajectories even after color classes merge. The update (a_i,b_j)->(a_i+1_{a_i+1 in R},b_j+1_{b_j+1 in L}) modulo four, applied simultaneously, exhausts the 15^2=225 initial shore-support pairs. Independently regenerated all 225 tagged histories and their ten (first-entry,least-period) populations 18,3,4,40,12,60,8,64,8,8 for (0,1),(0,4),(0,6),(1,1),(1,4),(2,1),(2,4),(3,1),(3,4),(4,1), respectively. The four period-six signatures are precisely 3-versus-3 initial supports; each has U_3(m)U_3(n) lifts, giving 4(3^m-3*2^m+3)(3^n-3*2^n+3). Nonzero C_(4,1)(2,3) and coexistence of periods 4 and 6 make 4-entry and 12-lag sharp when m,n>=3. The exhaustive tagged quotient, rather than finite-size vertex simulation, proves F^16=F^4 for all sizes. Boundary m=1 and n=1 are included by zero surjection factors.
